teaser: Underwriting an agent behaviour policy row by row: a limit per named risk, a lower premium per enforced control, and no cover for what is not named.
core_idea: An insurer de-risks an action up to a limit under conditions, and an agent behaviour policy already has that shape, so the insurance should be one-to-one with it: each row it names has its own limit, each row it does not name is excluded, each enforced control lowers that row's premium by a deterministic factor while a line in the prompt earns nothing, the runtime is part of the price, and the premium starts near the cover for an uncontrolled agent and falls with every real control.

nodes.label: A house against burglary
nodes.summary: Conditions, a limit per item, exclusions, and a check at the claim.

nodes.label: The behaviour policy as rows
nodes.summary: Grant, mandate and delta: each reachable capability is a row.

nodes.label: The delta is uninsurable
nodes.summary: Reach outside the mandate is what no policy covers, by design.

nodes.label: One row, one limit
nodes.summary: £20,000 for corrupted records, £50,000 for leaked data, and so on.

nodes.label: A deterministic formula
nodes.summary: Base rate times the factors of enforced controls times the runtime.

nodes.label: Only enforced controls count
nodes.summary: A hook, a proxy or a removed grant earns a factor; a prompt line does not.

nodes.label: 3 of 12 against 12 of 12
nodes.summary: The line alone against the line with a deny-all hook, in a drill.

nodes.label: Insurers price what they measure
nodes.summary: Black boxes for young drivers, medical underwriting, cyber scans.

nodes.label: Where the agent runs
nodes.summary: A certified runtime lowers the price; an uncertified one raises it.

nodes.label: The licence to operate
nodes.summary: Simulated in vault posrhzp3: band, ceiling, pool, premium.

nodes.label: The vendors' share
nodes.summary: Indemnities conditional on guardrails, performance guarantees, AIUC-1 cover.

nodes.summary: The next article in the series, a research brief.
